key_insight: A query-only LLM audit closely reproduced clinical prediction models and detected 96% of planted flaws, but its additional problem reports and discoveries required independent verification.
clinical_relevance: LLM audits may help inspect opaque clinical prediction tools, but these results do not establish clinical safety or improved patient outcomes.
method: Trained four model types on International Stroke Trial data for two outcomes.
Mixed 24 models with planted flaws and 8 clean models; GPT-6 Astra audited each three times using prediction queries only.
Applied pre-specified automated judging rules and tested unexpected relationships in later-randomised patients.
evidence_signal: Surrogates achieved mean log-odds R² of 0.976; the LLM detected 69/72 planted flaws across audit runs (96%; 95% CI 80–99%), while a purpose-written script detected all 24 flawed models.
watch_item: Of 1,089 checkable problem reports, 60% failed the pre-specified average-behaviour check; post hoc analysis found most were real but small steps, while 15% were absent from the model.
paper_title: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws
